currentContext.expansion: EIEL's expansion in FY 2025-26 was overwhelmingly platform- and acquisition-led rather than plant-capex-led, and the AR narrative describes it under 'Expansion Initiatives - Building New Platforms for Sustainable Growth'. In the core water business the Company continues to bid for and execute larger STP, CETP, sewerage and water-supply projects for government bodies, and is integrating Compressed Biogas (CBG) plants within STP projects to convert biogas from anaerobic sludge digestion for sale to oil marketing companies or on-site power generation, alongside advanced sludge treatment that classifies bio-solids into Class A/B/C resources for fertiliser or energy use. It is also building the commercial framework to resell tertiary-treated wastewater to thermal power plants and process industries under NGT-mandated purchase obligations, and is targeting ZLD mandates enabling industrial clusters to reuse more than 90% of treated wastewater. The second leg is the renewable platform under wholly owned subsidiary EIE Renewables: a solar portfolio scaled to 91 MW comprising 79 MW of IPP solar and 12 MW of EPC solar, which includes a recently acquired 40 MW IPP solar asset in Bolangir, Odisha and a 29 MW project under execution for MSEDCL in Maharashtra that carries state financial assistance of INR 32 million per MW and a 25-year PPA. In storage, EIEL secured four NTPC EPC orders aggregating 930 MWh and has commissioned a 150 MWh BESS IPP asset, for a combined 1,080 MWh portfolio. Wind was added post year-end through EIE Renewables' acquisition of Suyog Urja Limited for INR 3,110 million - described as asset-light and zero-debt - bringing 1,200 MW of completed wind execution experience, an active pipeline of 1,702 MW and an order book of approximately INR 7,770 million. The corporate structure was expanded accordingly during and after the year: EIE Renewables Private Limited (7 May 2025), Sunaxis Renewables Private Limited (6 June 2025), Soltrix Energy Solution Private Limited (25 June 2025, holding a 29 MW AC solar project), Vento Power Infra Private Limited (20 August 2025), and post year-end PRA Bihar Bess Private Limited (21 April 2026) and Suyog Urja Limited (28 April 2026). The recurring O&M portfolio stands at INR 9,506 million on contracts of up to 15 years post-commissioning. No rupee capex quantum is stated anywhere in this bundle: the capital-commitments named disclosure carries only its label line with no figure.

risks.risk: Total dependence on government funding cycles and policy priorities
risks.note: The BRSR material-issues table states that all the projects executed by the Company are funded by Central or State Government schemes, so changes in policy or funding priorities may impact project flow; the MD&A threats section adds that unexpected delays in central fund disbursements or shifts in budget allocations - as witnessed historically in certain rural missions, and specifically cited as historical delays under the Jal Jeevan Mission - may temporarily impact working capital cycles. Mitigation claimed is diversification across states and funding mechanisms, and concentrating the order book on ring-fenced schemes such as AMRUT 2.0, Namami Gange and multilateral agency-funded projects.

risks.risk: Working capital intensity of the EPC model
risks.note: The business requires significant upfront investment in procurement, mobilisation, subcontracting and workforce deployment while collections are linked to milestone-based billing and certification. Delays in customer payments, release of retention money or extended approval cycles lengthen the cash cycle and raise funding requirements, and management notes that executing larger projects and expanding the business may raise working capital intensity further. The Company says it targets a 90-day working capital cycle and keeps debt-to-equity at 0.3x; the reported Debt Equity Ratio nevertheless moved from 0.24 to 0.34 (a 41.67% variance), attributed to better utilisation of borrowings.

risks.risk: Cybersecurity, fraud and data integrity - a loss already crystallised in FY 2025-26
risks.note: This is not a hypothetical risk for EIEL: a cyber fraud incident occurred during the year, funds were traced and recovered through legal and banking channels, and the Company responded with a comprehensive overhaul of its IT security architecture, new SOPs, multi-tier authorisation protocols, multi-tiered digital firewalls, a review of financial approval workflows and mandatory continuous cybersecurity training. As operations digitise further, fraud attempts and data breaches remain a threat to financial and operational stability.

risks.risk: Execution and operational complexity on increasingly large and technical projects
risks.note: Executing complex ZLD systems and large-scale renewable EPC mandates carries risk of cost overruns, delays and third-party subcontractor failures. The stated mitigant is the fully in-house engineering, procurement and execution model that removes reliance on subcontractors - and management explicitly ties this to protecting its guided 22% to 24% EBITDA margins, so an execution slip transmits directly to the margin guidance. The BRSR material-issues table separately flags construction and execution risks covering project delays, cost escalation and supply chain disruption.

risks.risk: Regulatory and environmental compliance under NGT and CPCB norms
risks.note: The water and renewable sectors are highly regulated, with stringent discharge norms enforced by the National Green Tribunal and Central Pollution Control Board. The BRSR table notes non-compliance may lead to penalties, project delays or reputational impact, with negative financial implications from compliance costs and potential penalties. The Company relies on in-house design to build STPs and CETPs that exceed current standards, aiming to future-proof assets against evolving environmental law.

risks.risk: Land acquisition, right-of-way and local clearance delays
risks.note: Infrastructure projects inherently face delays in land acquisition, right-of-way approvals and local clearances - factors outside the Company's control that may extend execution timelines and, critically for an EPC recognising revenue on progress, delay revenue recognition.

risks.risk: Grid non-availability, evacuation bottlenecks and technology obsolescence in the new renewable vertical
risks.note: For the renewable ventures, delays in state-level grid infrastructure and transmission connectivity may affect timely commissioning and power evacuation for both IPP and EPC solar/wind assets. Separately, the rapid evolution of BESS and renewable hybrid technologies creates a technological obsolescence risk. Mitigation is a technology-agnostic approach with multiple leading global OEMs and rigorous pre-bid site assessments to confirm evacuation infrastructure before committing.

risks.risk: Supply chain and raw material price volatility, plus interest rate exposure
risks.note: As an infrastructure developer the Company is exposed to price movements in steel and cement and in specialised components such as RO membranes and BESS battery cells, mitigated through price escalation clauses in long-term contracts wherever feasible and strategic supplier tie-ups. Working capital borrowings are benchmarked to RBI-regulated reference rates such as REPO or Treasury Bills, so rate increases raise borrowing costs; interest rate scenarios are factored into project costing at the bidding stage.

risks.risk: Credit concentration on public-sector receivables and intense competitive bidding
risks.note: Credit risk arises mainly from receivables under EPC and O&M contracts executed for public sector clients - government bodies, urban development authorities and state-led infrastructure agencies - with contracts typically backed by budgetary allocations or multilateral funding. At the same time the attractiveness of the water utility and renewable sectors continues to draw domestic and international entrants, producing aggressive bidding environments that require strict margin discipline.

one-line thesis: Pure-play water/wastewater EPC missed FY26 revenue guidance (35%→7.5% growth) on slow order finalization + projects stuck in design stage, but pivots hard into renewables (BESS/wind/solar, now ~35-40% of order book) with all-time-high INR6,814 cr total order book giving ~24-month visibility — execution conversion (not order book) is the swing factor, and a global commodity crisis trims FY27 margin guidance.
financial scorecard:
**Q4 FY26:** Revenue INR427.3 cr (+8.8% YoY); EBITDA INR79.9 cr, margin 18.7% (weakest margins of year); PAT INR54.3 cr, PAT margin 12.4%.
**FY26 (full year):** Revenue INR1,145.6 cr (+7.5% YoY — MISSED ~35% guidance); EBITDA INR276.8 cr (+3.4%), margin 24.2%; PAT INR188.4 cr, margin 15.9%.
- **Order book (all-time high): INR6,814 cr total** = Water/WW execution INR2,733 cr + Water/WW O&M INR951 cr + Renewable execution INR2,051 cr + Renewable O&M/IPP INR1,079 cr. **Execution-only OB = INR4,800 cr** (Water/WW ~INR2,700 cr + Renewables ~INR2,050 cr).
- **Book-to-bill:** ~4.2x on execution OB / ~6x total OB vs FY26 revenue — gives clear 2-year (FY27+FY28) visibility.
- **Net debt:** Total debt INR422 cr (long-term/term-loan-HAM INR250 cr + short-term/CC ~INR175 cr). **D/E = 0.34x.** Finance cost DIPPED YoY.
- **Working capital: STRETCHED to 166 days** (vs 95-100 target). Split: inventory 11d, receivables 53d (improved), **UBR 195d (blowout)**, creditors 92d. Cause: AMRUT funds not released (Chhattisgarh, MP, Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab) → cannot raise GST invoices.
- **Cash flow:** OCF pre-tax ~breakeven (+INR4 lakh); post-tax INR-63 cr (negative, partly from 15-yr service-concession/HAM receivables booked to OCF per accounting policy). Mgmt calls "adjusted OCF" positive.
- **One-offs / drags in Q4:** ~INR100-120 cr renewable IPP revenue at ~0% margin; ECL provision INR10 cr (Ind AS); depreciation up ~INR25 cr (new construction equipment); employee cost up to ~6% of revenue (+~1.5pp, projects sat in design stage so cost booked w/o revenue). Cost of manufacturing actually DOWN ~1pp.
guidance (critical):
- **FY27 revenue: ~INR2,000 cr** (vs INR1,145 cr FY26 — implies ~75% growth, but mgmt frames as ~42% conversion of INR4,800 cr execution OB, deliberately conservative). Split: Water/WW ~INR1,350 cr + Renewables ~INR650 cr.
- **FY27 PAT: INR270-280 cr; PAT margin ~13.5-14%** (blended).
- **FY27 EBITDA margin: LOWERED to 21-22%** (from earlier 22-24%) due to global commodity/geopolitical crisis (1-2pp hit; price-variation clauses cover only part).
- **FY27 order inflow target: at least INR2,500 cr** of fresh orders.
- **FY28: 35-40% topline growth** implied; ~INR2,500-2,800 cr revenue from remaining current OB — "FY27 & FY28 visibility clear on current OB."
- **Q1 FY27 color:** Better than Q1 FY26 (~INR250 cr) despite global crisis; no number given.
- **Renewables/BESS margin:** BESS EPC ~10% PAT; blended renewables 10-12% PAT.
order book & pipeline:
- Execution OB INR4,800 cr; total OB INR6,814 cr (incl. O&M + IPP).
- Q4 additions: BUIDCO Bihar INR348 cr; Pune+Nashik sanitation (Swachh Bharat) INR824 cr; 4 NTPC BESS EPC projects (930 MWh, ~INR1,070 cr — UP/Assam/Karnataka/Telangana); acquired 150 MWh BESS project in Bihar.
- **Bid pipeline:** ~INR1,200 cr bids submitted + ~INR5,000 cr of projects of interest yet to bid.

segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Water/WW EPC (core):** STP (per-MLD INR1-1.5 cr), CETP (INR2-15 cr/MLD, industry-dependent), WTP (INR30-50 lakh/MLD). Design = 2-5% of turnkey value. Mostly EPC; some STPs on HAM. Completed marquee projects: 100 MLD STP Jodhpur (IFAS + biogas power + UF), 55 MLD STP Varanasi (solar-on-reactor, India-first, NMCG-recognized), 25 MLD CETP Sarigam, 30 MLD STP Bhiwadi — raising pre-qualification for larger/complex plants.
- **O&M (Water/WW):** INR951 cr OB; 3-5% of revenue; higher margin than execution; growing in absolute terms YoY.
- **Renewables (1 yr old):** Execution OB INR2,051 cr + O&M/IPP INR1,079 cr. NTPC BESS EPC (incl. EHV transformers / HT transmission lines self-executed). Wind EPC via **Suyog Urja Ltd** (acquired) — serves A-to-AAA-rated private clients. Solar assets + IPP. Reported as separate company; segmental revenues to be disclosed separately going forward.
growth verticals / optionality:
- BESS: positioning as first-mover in India's 90 GW battery-storage pipeline; 930 MWh NTPC + 150 MWh Bihar.
- Wind EPC (Suyog) into private A/AAA clients — de-risks govt receivables.
- Desalination optionality: MIDC CETP-ZLD textile project (UF/RO, one of India's biggest) builds pre-qualification to enter desalination (open to JVs).
- Water re-use / BOT: treated CETP/ZLD water recirculated to industry could become revenue stream / BOT model (preliminary).
- T&D EPC: NOT entering soon, but BESS work (EHV/HT lines) gives pre-quals; possible future diversification (AI-driven power demand cited).
- HAM/IPP annuity income — decent IRR, O&M absolute profitability rising.
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 EBITDA margin 24.2% (mgmt says no real compression once normalized; Q4 18.7% optical due to 0-margin IPP revenue + ECL + depreciation + design-stage employee cost). FY27 EBITDA guided 21-22% (cut 1-2pp for commodity inflation). Price-variation clauses in most contracts offset PART of cost rises, not all. BESS EPC ~10% PAT (lithium-ion import cost pressure — deferring battery procurement, doing BOS/civil/electrical first).
capex / expansion: Light. Per new project ~INR4-5 cr equipment (reuse first). Total FY27 capex ~INR20-30 cr, "not a bigger amount." Watch: execution slippage — FY26 miss was ~INR100 cr each from renewables and wastewater stuck in design/approval (Bangalore x2, MIDC CETP-ZLD).
capital allocation: D/E 0.34x; max comfort 1:1 consolidated (incl. renewable development projects). Finance cost down YoY. Asset monetization/offloading planned if leverage runs heavy (has solar/IPP assets). Disciplined, complementary diversification stance.
risks & watch-items:
- **Govt-payment cycle:** AMRUT funds not released (5-6 states) → UBR ballooned to 195d, WC to 166d; recurring (Jal Jeevan last yr, AMRUT this yr). Some releases now confirmed (Chhattisgarh; coming for Rajasthan/Haryana/MP).
- **Order finalization delays / re-bidding:** elongated bid evaluation; a Nov-Dec L1 project went to re-bid (timeline lost, neutral outcome).
- **Commodity / geopolitical crisis:** raw-material/lithium-ion cost spike → 1-2pp margin pressure.
- **Guidance credibility:** missed FY26 35% guidance; investor explicitly asked for realistic targets — FY27 deliberately conservative.
- **OCF post-tax negative** (-INR63 cr); concentration on central-govt-funded projects (de-risking via NTPC B2B + private wind).
management quality / tone: Candid on the miss — admitted revenue guidance not met, explained design-stage cost build-up, ECL/depreciation/IPP drags transparently. Conservative reframing of FY27 (42% conversion vs raw 75% growth). Took investor criticism on guidance realism gracefully. Confident but measured on renewables; disciplined leverage and capex discipline. Slightly defensive on "no margin compression" framing.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The headline "+75% FY27 growth" is an artifact of a tiny FY26 base; mgmt insists on viewing it as ~42% OB conversion — the real number to track is conversion rate, not growth %.
- FY26 ~95% order-to-order conversion but revenue still missed — the bottleneck is design/approval-to-execution lag, not order wins.
- Renewables grew from ~INR12 cr (till Dec) to INR117 cr in Q4 alone — entire FY26 renewable revenue (INR129 cr) was back-ended and ~0-margin (IPP), structurally depressing Q4 optics.
- UBR at 195 days (not receivables — receivables actually improved to 53d) is the true working-capital story; it's GST-invoice timing tied to govt fund release, so a release wave could sharply unwind WC.
- Company is quietly building T&D/transmission pre-quals via BESS execution — optionality not yet priced.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- A substantial portion of the order book was in design, engineering and early mobilisation during FY 2025-26 - stages that are capital and management-intensive but contribute minimally to revenue recognition; as construction advances through FY 2026-27, revenue recognition is expected to mirror the scale of the underlying order book.
- EBITDA margin of 24.2% is described as consistent with the Company's stated guidance for the water and wastewater segment.
- Structural water demand: the Indian wastewater treatment market is supported by an estimated immediate bid pipeline exceeding INR 26,000 crore under AMRUT 2.0 alone, and the sector is described as structurally positioned for sustained double-digit growth.
- The future landscape is expected to be dominated by Hybrid Annuity Models and 'One City, One Operator' frameworks, enabling long-term operational efficiency and stable annuity yields for EPC players.
- NGT enforcement of stringent ZLD guidelines and mandated purchase of treated sewage water by thermal power plants is expected to raise industrial demand for complex tertiary treatment and desalination equipment.
- Centrally funded missions - AMRUT 2.0 (INR 2.77 lakh crore outlay, mandating cities meet at least 20% of water demand and 40% of industrial water demand from reuse), Namami Gange Phase-II (INR 22,500 crore through 2026, HAM and 15-year O&M), and SBM-U 2.0 (INR 1.41 lakh crore, FSSM in Tier 2/3 cities) - provide long-term visibility and execution scale.
- Sector shift from disposal to recycling, reuse and resource recovery: sludge classification and valorisation, resale of tertiary-treated water, and on-site biogas/rooftop solar energy integration to offset aeration and pumping energy costs.
- Renewables: India targets 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030; the CEA projects a requirement of nearly 42 GW (208 GWh) of BESS capacity by FY 2029-30, and Viability Gap Funding supports early BESS project viability.
- The renewable sector is moving beyond standalone solar parks towards hybridisation and storage; developers able to integrate wind, solar and BESS gain a competitive advantage through 24/7 supply and reduced grid imbalance.
- Wind: India's cumulative installed wind capacity crossed 56 GW by end FY 2025-26 with a record 6.05 GW added, against a government target of 100 GW by 2030, with the pipeline increasingly shaped by Wind-Solar Hybrid tenders.
- Threats management flags as affecting the outlook: land acquisition, right-of-way and clearance delays extending execution timelines; grid non-availability and evacuation bottlenecks delaying renewable commissioning; dependency on government funding cycles affecting working capital; and intense competition producing aggressive bidding that requires strict margin discipline.
- Consolidated order book of INR 68,136 million entering FY 2026-27, up 242% year-on-year, driven by key water EPC wins and the addition of the Suyog Urja order book.
- The year opened with an order book of approximately INR 11,855 million, most of which was still progressing through design, engineering and early mobilisation.
- O&M portfolio at INR 9,506 million, covering long-term contracts that generate recurring, annuity-based revenue independent of new project awards.
- Major FY 2025-26 order wins: INR 3,955 million ZLD CETP for MIDC in Maharashtra, INR 3,484 million STP project from Bihar Urban Infrastructure Development Corporation Ltd., and INR 2,480 million urban sewerage project from Municipal Corporation Bhopal.
- Renewable orders: four NTPC BESS EPC contracts aggregating 930 MWh across Uttar Pradesh, Assam, Karnataka and Telangana, plus a 150 MWh BESS IPP asset (1,080 MWh combined).
- Suyog Urja brings an order book of approximately INR 7,770 million and an active wind execution pipeline of 1,702 MW.
- Management states the healthy order pipeline and disciplined execution provide strong forward visibility, with existing order inflows supporting medium-term growth expectations under conservative conversion assumptions.

capex_expansion.body: EIEL's expansion in FY 2025-26 was overwhelmingly platform- and acquisition-led rather than plant-capex-led, and the AR narrative describes it under 'Expansion Initiatives - Building New Platforms for Sustainable Growth'. In the core water business the Company continues to bid for and execute larger STP, CETP, sewerage and water-supply projects for government bodies, and is integrating Compressed Biogas (CBG) plants within STP projects to convert biogas from anaerobic sludge digestion for sale to oil marketing companies or on-site power generation, alongside advanced sludge treatment that classifies bio-solids into Class A/B/C resources for fertiliser or energy use. It is also building the commercial framework to resell tertiary-treated wastewater to thermal power plants and process industries under NGT-mandated purchase obligations, and is targeting ZLD mandates enabling industrial clusters to reuse more than 90% of treated wastewater. The second leg is the renewable platform under wholly owned subsidiary EIE Renewables: a solar portfolio scaled to 91 MW comprising 79 MW of IPP solar and 12 MW of EPC solar, which includes a recently acquired 40 MW IPP solar asset in Bolangir, Odisha and a 29 MW project under execution for MSEDCL in Maharashtra that carries state financial assistance of INR 32 million per MW and a 25-year PPA. In storage, EIEL secured four NTPC EPC orders aggregating 930 MWh and has commissioned a 150 MWh BESS IPP asset, for a combined 1,080 MWh portfolio. Wind was added post year-end through EIE Renewables' acquisition of Suyog Urja Limited for INR 3,110 million - described as asset-light and zero-debt - bringing 1,200 MW of completed wind execution experience, an active pipeline of 1,702 MW and an order book of approximately INR 7,770 million. The corporate structure was expanded accordingly during and after the year: EIE Renewables Private Limited (7 May 2025), Sunaxis Renewables Private Limited (6 June 2025), Soltrix Energy Solution Private Limited (25 June 2025, holding a 29 MW AC solar project), Vento Power Infra Private Limited (20 August 2025), and post year-end PRA Bihar Bess Private Limited (21 April 2026) and Suyog Urja Limited (28 April 2026). The recurring O&M portfolio stands at INR 9,506 million on contracts of up to 15 years post-commissioning. No rupee capex quantum is stated anywhere in this bundle: the capital-commitments named disclosure carries only its label line with no figure.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Candid on the miss — admitted revenue guidance not met, explained design-stage cost build-up, ECL/depreciation/IPP drags transparently. Conservative reframing of FY27 (42% conversion vs raw 75% growth). Took investor criticism on guidance realism gracefully. Confident but measured on renewables; disciplined leverage and capex discipline. Slightly defensive on "no margin compression" framing.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- In-house design, engineering and process capability with specialised civil contractors only for site execution - stated to ensure quality control, reduce margin leakage and enable timely delivery
- Asset-light balance sheet discipline: debt-to-equity of 0.3x, kept well below 1.0x, with a selective HAM alongside EPC mix
- Track record moat: 57 projects and 958 MLD of cumulative treatment capacity since 2009, promoters with 53 years of cumulative experience and a 35+ year track record in water and wastewater management
- Established Zero Liquid Discharge and tertiary treatment capability, positioning the Company for NGT-driven reuse mandates
- Recurring, high-margin annuity revenue from post-commissioning O&M contracts running 1 to 15 years
- Early-mover position in BESS built by clearing complex technical pre-qualifications for early utility-scale tenders, giving 1,080 MWh of secured capacity
- Trademarks 'EiE' and 'Empowering Green Planet', with 100% in-house engineering and design plus ERP/IT frameworks described as the primary competitive moat

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Govt-payment cycle:** AMRUT funds not released (5-6 states) → UBR ballooned to 195d, WC to 166d; recurring (Jal Jeevan last yr, AMRUT this yr). Some releases now confirmed (Chhattisgarh; coming for Rajasthan/Haryana/MP).
- **Order finalization delays / re-bidding:** elongated bid evaluation; a Nov-Dec L1 project went to re-bid (timeline lost, neutral outcome).
- **Commodity / geopolitical crisis:** raw-material/lithium-ion cost spike → 1-2pp margin pressure.
- **Guidance credibility:** missed FY26 35% guidance; investor explicitly asked for realistic targets — FY27 deliberately conservative.
- **OCF post-tax negative** (-INR63 cr); concentration on central-govt-funded projects (de-risking via NTPC B2B + private wind).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The headline "+75% FY27 growth" is an artifact of a tiny FY26 base; mgmt insists on viewing it as ~42% OB conversion — the real number to track is conversion rate, not growth %.
- FY26 ~95% order-to-order conversion but revenue still missed — the bottleneck is design/approval-to-execution lag, not order wins.
- Renewables grew from ~INR12 cr (till Dec) to INR117 cr in Q4 alone — entire FY26 renewable revenue (INR129 cr) was back-ended and ~0-margin (IPP), structurally depressing Q4 optics.
- UBR at 195 days (not receivables — receivables actually improved to 53d) is the true working-capital story; it's GST-invoice timing tied to govt fund release, so a release wave could sharply unwind WC.
- Company is quietly building T&D/transmission pre-quals via BESS execution — optionality not yet priced.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Run two structurally separate growth engines - water and wastewater infrastructure on EBITDA-driven EPC and O&M economics, and renewable energy under wholly owned subsidiary EIE Renewables on EPC margins plus IRR-linked IPP returns - deliberately kept as independent operating and reporting units so different business models and risk profiles are not blurred.
- Move up the value chain by bidding for and executing larger, more technically complex projects with higher margin potential; execution capability has been expanded from 50 to 200 MLD for STPs and 20 to 50 MLD for CETPs.

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log
qoq_log.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this):** All-time-high total OB INR6,814 cr (exec INR4,800 cr). FY26 revenue INR1,145 cr (+7.5%, MISSED 35% guidance); FY26 EBITDA margin 24.2%, PAT INR188 cr.
